newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat says 96 normal profits below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says 96 normal profits below forecasts.

text.p: Italian automotive and industrial group Fiat said that its 1996 profits from normal activities will be below previous forecasts.
But the group said in a statement that the second half of 1996 will see extraordinary gains.
Fiat said the fall in its first half pretax 1996 figure reflected lower operating profits and the lack of extraodinary gains which had boosted first-half pretax 1995 profits.

The group said its lower operating profits were due to a small contribution from its Brazilian operations, the rise in the lira against other major currencies, the difficulty in raising prices, and the costs in the first quarter of launching new models at Fiat Auto and New Holland tractors and farm machinery unit.

Fiat's first-half pretax 1996 profit fell to 1.547 trillion lire from 2.153 trillion lire, while stripping out extraordinary gains the pretax fall was reduced to a first half pretax figure of 1.538 trillion lire in 1996 from 1.761 trillion lire in the first half of 1995.
Group sources said that the appreciation of the lira caused a reduction of 450 billion lire in the pretax figure.
